grammar.title: Move words to shift the emphasis
grammar.intro: Spanish word order is flexible, and advanced speakers exploit that to shift emphasis away from neutral subject–verb–object. You can front an object (El pan lo compré yo), lift a topic to the front (De dinero, no hablemos) or front an adjective (Muy interesante fue la charla). The one hard rule: when you front a direct object, a matching clitic pronoun must stay behind.

sections.heading: Front the object, keep a clitic
sections.body: You may move the direct object to the front for emphasis, but a matching clitic pronoun must remain in its usual place: El pan lo compré yo (The bread, I bought). Drop the clitic and the sentence is ungrammatical for native ears.

sections.heading: The clitic must agree
sections.body: Pick the clitic that matches the fronted object in gender and number — lo, la, los, las. When the object is a specific person it keeps its personal a as well: A María la vi ayer (María, I saw yesterday). Standard usage uses la/lo, not le, for the direct object.

ex.en: Your parents, I called (them) last night.
The keys, I left (them) at home.

sections.heading: Topic first, comment after
sections.body: You can lift a whole theme to the front — often after a preposition — and then comment on it: De dinero, no hablemos (As for money, let's not talk about it). Markers like en cuanto a and por lo que respecta a announce the topic before the sentence proper.

ex.en: As for politics, better not to talk.

sections.heading: Fronting adjectives, adverbs & afterthoughts
sections.body: Moving an adjective or adverb to the front adds emphasis or a literary tone: Muy interesante fue la charla (Very interesting was the talk). Right-dislocation instead tacks a clarifying element onto the end: Ya lo sabía, lo del despido.

ex.en: I already knew — about the layoff.

takeaways: Front a direct object and you must add a matching clitic: El pan lo compré yo.
The clitic agrees in gender and number: lo, la, los, las.
A specific-person object keeps its personal a: A María la vi.
Topicalization (De dinero, no hablemos) and fronted adjectives (Muy interesante fue…) mark emphasis.

mistakes.why: A fronted direct object requires a resumptive clitic: lo.
A fronted personal object still needs its clitic: la.

mistakes.w: Las llaves los dejé en casa.
mistakes.r: Las llaves las dejé en casa.
mistakes.why: The clitic must agree with llaves (feminine plural): las, not los.

exercises.no: The fronted object el pan needs the matching clitic lo.
The direct-object clitic for María is la (standard usage avoids leísmo 'le').

exercises.prompt: Build: “The keys, I left at home.”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Las llaves las dejé — clitic agrees.
exercises.no: “Las llaves las dejé en casa” — the clitic las doubles the fronted object.

exercises.prompt_en: Your parents, I called (them) last night.
exercises.hint: Clitic agreeing with a masculine-plural person.
exercises.no: The fronted object needs the clitic los: “A tus padres los llamé”.

exercises.prompt: Match each fronted object to its clitic.

exercises.translation: As for money, let's not talk about it.
exercises.no: It was: “De dinero, no hablemos.” (As for money, let's not talk about it.)

exercises.scenario: Sorting out who bought the bread 🥖

lines.speaker: Sofía
lines.es: ¿Compraste tú el pan o lo compró Marcos?
lines.en: Did you buy the bread, or did Marcos buy it?

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! El pan lo compré yo — clitic kept.
exercises.no: A fronted object needs its clitic: “El pan lo compré yo”.
Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the sound of “A María la vi ayer.”
